method: Same demo-shop questions via (a) GraneKernel.query — the MCP query tool — and (b) handwritten SQL through pg / DuckDB, not Grane. Relative periods anchored to max(orders timestamps). Independent SQL is the metric definition, never compiler output.

questions.question: What was Revenue last month?
questions.note: Booked on completed_at, status = completed. Relative period is last_month.

grane.sql:
/* grane query_id=q_37d9b8919cf7 agent=- */
SELECT SUM("orders"."net_amount") FILTER (WHERE "orders"."status" = $1) AS "revenue",
       COUNT(*) OVER() AS "__grane_n",
       1 AS "__grane_row"
FROM "orders"
WHERE "orders"."completed_at" >= $2::timestamp
  AND "orders"."completed_at" < $3::timestamp
LIMIT 1000

raw.sql:
SELECT SUM(net_amount) AS revenue FROM orders
         WHERE status = 'completed'
           AND completed_at >= '2026-09-01'::timestamp AND completed_at < '2026-10-01'::timestamp

questions.question: What is our average order value?
questions.note: Ratio of SUM(net_amount) / COUNT(*) on completed orders, not AVG(net_amount) over every row.

grane.sql:
/* grane query_id=q_fb0bc08ad7cb agent=- */
SELECT (SUM("orders"."net_amount") FILTER (WHERE "orders"."status" = $1))::numeric / NULLIF((COUNT("orders"."id") FILTER (WHERE "orders"."status" = $2))::numeric, 0) AS "average_order_value",
       COUNT(*) OVER() AS "__grane_n",
       1 AS "__grane_row"
FROM "orders"
LIMIT 1000

raw.sql:
SELECT CAST(SUM(net_amount) AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS average_order_value
         FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed'

questions.question: Revenue by country.

grane.sql:
/* grane query_id=q_16d917898a03 agent=- */
WITH "__grane_pop" AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM "orders"
),
"__grane_contrib" AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM "__grane_pop" AS "orders"
  WHERE ("orders"."status" = $1)
),
"__grane_reach_customers" AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM "customers"
  WHERE "customers"."id" IN (
    SELECT "orders"."customer_id" FROM "__grane_contrib" AS "orders" WHERE "orders"."customer_id" IS NOT NULL)
),
"__grane_card" AS (
  SELECT (SELECT MAX("_n") FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS "_n" FROM "__grane_reach_customers" GROUP BY "id") AS "_keys") AS "__grane_card_customers"
  FROM (SELECT 1 AS "_x") AS "_grane_one"
),
"__grane_result" AS (
  SELECT "customers"."country" AS "country",
         SUM("orders"."net_amount") FILTER (WHERE "orders"."status" = $2) AS "revenue",
         COUNT(*) OVER() AS "__grane_n",
         1 AS "__grane_row"
  FROM "__grane_pop" AS "orders"
  LEFT JOIN "customers" ON "orders"."customer_id" = "customers"."id"
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY "revenue" DESC
  LIMIT 1000
)
SELECT "__grane_result"."country",
       "__grane_result"."revenue",
       "__grane_result"."__grane_n",
       "__grane_result"."__grane_row",
       "__grane_card"."__grane_card_customers"
FROM "__grane_card"
LEFT JOIN "__grane_result" ON TRUE
ORDER BY "__grane_result"."revenue" DESC

raw.sql:
SELECT c.country, SUM(o.net_amount) AS revenue
         FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
         WHERE o.status = 'completed'
         GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

questions.question: How much did we collect in succeeded payments, by country?
questions.note: Payments are one-to-many from orders; independent SQL pre-aggregates at order grain before joining customers.

grane.sql:
/* grane query_id=q_76da512ae407 agent=- */
WITH "m_payments_received" AS (
  SELECT "payments"."order_id" AS "_key", SUM("payments"."amount") AS "value"
  FROM "payments"
  WHERE "payments"."status" = $1
  GROUP BY "payments"."order_id"
),
"__grane_pop" AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM "orders"
),
"__grane_reach_customers" AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM "customers"
  WHERE "customers"."id" IN (
    SELECT "orders"."customer_id" FROM "__grane_pop" AS "orders" WHERE "orders"."customer_id" IS NOT NULL)
),
"__grane_card" AS (
  SELECT (SELECT MAX("_n") FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS "_n" FROM "__grane_reach_customers" GROUP BY "id") AS "_keys") AS "__grane_card_customers"
  FROM (SELECT 1 AS "_x") AS "_grane_one"
),
"__grane_result" AS (
  SELECT "customers"."country" AS "country",
         SUM("m_payments_received"."value") AS "payments_received",
         COUNT(*) OVER() AS "__grane_n",
         1 AS "__grane_row"
  FROM "__grane_pop" AS "orders"
  LEFT JOIN "customers" ON "orders"."customer_id" = "customers"."id"
  LEFT JOIN "m_payments_received" ON "m_payments_received"."_key" = "orders"."id"
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY "payments_received" DESC
  LIMIT 1000
)
SELECT "__grane_result"."country",
       "__grane_result"."payments_received",
       "__grane_result"."__grane_n",
       "__grane_result"."__grane_row",
       "__grane_card"."__grane_card_customers"
FROM "__grane_card"
LEFT JOIN "__grane_result" ON TRUE
ORDER BY "__grane_result"."payments_received" DESC

raw.sql:
SELECT c.country, SUM(p.value) AS payments_received
         FROM orders o
         JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
         LEFT JOIN (
           SELECT order_id, SUM(amount) AS value FROM payments
           WHERE status = 'succeeded' GROUP BY 1
         ) p ON p.order_id = o.id
         GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

questions.question: Show revenue and payments received side by side.
questions.note: Independent SQL uses two scalar subqueries so the payment fan-out cannot multiply revenue.

grane.sql:
/* grane query_id=q_d0d29801a485 agent=- */
WITH "m_payments_received" AS (
  SELECT "payments"."order_id" AS "_key", SUM("payments"."amount") AS "value"
  FROM "payments"
  WHERE "payments"."status" = $1
  GROUP BY "payments"."order_id"
)
SELECT SUM("orders"."net_amount") FILTER (WHERE "orders"."status" = $2) AS "revenue",
       SUM("m_payments_received"."value") AS "payments_received",
       COUNT(*) OVER() AS "__grane_n",
       1 AS "__grane_row"
FROM "orders"
LEFT JOIN "m_payments_received" ON "m_payments_received"."_key" = "orders"."id"
LIMIT 1000

raw.sql:
SELECT
           (SELECT SUM(net_amount) FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed') AS revenue,
           (SELECT SUM(amount) FROM payments WHERE status = 'succeeded') AS payments_received

questions.question: Revenue by product category.
questions.note: Order-grain revenue joined through order_items fans out. Grane should refuse; raw SQL still returns a number.

grane.message: Joining dimension "product_category" requires traversing "orders" -> "order_items" (one_to_many), which would multiply rows at the metric grain ("orders") and corrupt aggregation. Grane refuses this query. Define a metric at the "products" grain instead.

raw.sql:
SELECT p.category, SUM(o.net_amount) AS revenue
         FROM orders o
         JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
         JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
         WHERE o.status = 'completed'
         GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

questions.question: Revenue by support ticket category.

grane.message: Joining raw dimension "support_tickets.category" requires traversing "customers" -> "support_tickets" (one_to_many), which would multiply rows at the metric grain ("orders") and corrupt aggregation. Grane refuses this query. Define a metric at the "support_tickets" grain instead.

raw.sql:
SELECT t.category, SUM(o.net_amount) AS revenue
         FROM orders o
         JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
         JOIN support_tickets t ON t.customer_id = c.id
         WHERE o.status = 'completed'
         GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

questions.question: Revenue by checkout event type.

grane.message: Joining raw dimension "checkout_events.event_type" requires traversing "orders" -> "checkout_events" (one_to_many), which would multiply rows at the metric grain ("orders") and corrupt aggregation. Grane refuses this query. Define a metric at the "checkout_events" grain instead.

raw.sql:
SELECT e.event_type, SUM(o.net_amount) AS revenue
         FROM orders o JOIN checkout_events e ON e.order_id = o.id
         WHERE o.status = 'completed'
         GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

       "__grane_result"."__grane_row",
       "__grane_card"."__grane_card_customers"
FROM "__grane_card"
LEFT JOIN "__grane_result" ON TRUE
ORDER BY "__grane_result"."payments_received" DESC

raw.sql:
SELECT c.country, SUM(p.value) AS payments_received
         FROM orders o
         JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
         LEFT JOIN (
           SELECT order_id, SUM(amount) AS value FROM payments
           WHERE status = 'succeeded' GROUP BY 1
         ) p ON p.order_id = o.id

questions.note: Independent SQL uses two scalar subqueries so the payment fan-out cannot multiply revenue.

WITH "m_payments_received" AS (
  SELECT "payments"."order_id" AS "_key", SUM("payments"."amount") AS "value"
  FROM "grane_cons_mvch8hkw_5sd7o8"."payments"
  WHERE "payments"."status" = $1
  GROUP BY "payments"."order_id"
)

       SUM("m_payments_received"."value") AS "payments_received",
       COUNT(*) OVER() AS "__grane_n",
       1 AS "__grane_row"
FROM "grane_cons_mvch8hkw_5sd7o8"."orders"
LEFT JOIN "m_payments_received" ON "m_payments_received"."_key" = "orders"."id"
LIMIT 1000

questions.question: Revenue by product category.
questions.note: Order-grain revenue joined through order_items fans out. Grane should refuse; raw SQL still returns a number.

grane.message: Joining dimension "product_category" requires traversing "orders" -> "order_items" (one_to_many), which would multiply rows at the metric grain ("orders") and corrupt aggregation. Grane refuses this query. Define a metric at the "products" grain instead.

raw.sql:
SELECT p.category, SUM(o.net_amount) AS revenue
         FROM orders o
         JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
         JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
         WHERE o.status = 'completed'
         GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC
